notes: Rule edit; replaces the 'life peer sits in the House of Commons' edit. Review fix (main_fix): that edit had an unedited superclass route back to the old value (a life peer is a peer, and peers sit in the Lords), so its 'determinate' queries were not determinate, and its well-known members (Thatcher, Olivier) came with worlds that denied the bridges the record required. The new rule has no more general rule that re-derives 'four years' for a US president: the term follows from nothing else, and no unedited fact about presidents in general (or about elected heads of state) gives four years. Derivability very_unlikely: stated directly and everywhere. R1: a president who succeeds mid-term serves out the remainder, but the term itself is four years; the Twenty-second Amendment limits the number of terms, not their length. Six years: plausible (Mexico, and the Senate's term) and clearly false. The near query asks the House's term (two years), another US office under the same relation, so an edit that spread to US offices in general would show. All three derived queries name a fictional president in the prompt, so the rule is the only route (inheritance, 2 hops); the third is an application (setting a countdown). The unedited facts are not about these people at all. Evidence: Wikipedia was queried once for the quote (the lead); later requests were refused with 429, so the other records lean on Dolma counts alone. Propositional: negation worded 'Is it true that it is not the case that ...'; the conjunction's side fact (Newton) is true, the disjunction's (Norway in South America) false, each with a check.
